clue.text: Clothing a couple of unknowns, tailor had a stylistic mode of floral design

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the pair of unknowns like a garment around a body
to tailor is to cut and refashion, so these letters are remade into a new order

parts.note: x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns; two of them here are Z and Y

explanation.surface: A dressmaker with a flair for style creates a flowery embroidered pattern on a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor' looks like the dressmaker of the surface but is the signal to rearrange; 'Clothing' wraps that mixed result around the two algebra letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an embroidery stitch made of loops arranged like petals, used to work flower patterns.

clue.text: Cavalryman admitting first parts of puzzle difficult, attempts the teaser

indicators.note: the cavalry soldier lets the initials in, so they sit inside his word

parts.note: a lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier, struggling with a hard puzzle, tries to tease it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the teaser' looks like a puzzle, but it is a performer who teases a club audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic dancer who performs close to a seated customer is a tease by profession.

clue.text: Liquorice flavouring (seedless) in relish, most nutty

indicators.note: the trimmed flavouring sits inside the word for relish

parts.note: zest is keen enjoyment, gusto

indicators.note: the word for the flavouring loses its closing 'seed'

parts.note: aniseed gives the liquorice-like taste to many sweets

explanation.surface: A recipe note: aniseed, minus its seeds, goes into a relish to make it as nutty as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most nutty' sounds culinary but means most crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty in the sense of crazy or wacky, so the superlative is the wackiest or most clownish.

clue.text: High table with odd locking device

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are in a muddled state

explanation.surface: At a college dinner, the top table has a strange lock fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High table' reads as one phrase at a formal dinner, but 'High' is the signal to rearrange TABLE and ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbolt is a bolt moved by turning a key, with no spring, used to secure a door.

clue.text: Thought control in the end proving visionary

parts.note: an idea is a thought

indicators.note: only the final letter of control is kept

explanation.surface: Keeping one's thinking in check ultimately proves to be far-sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionary as an adjective means existing as an imagined perfection, utopian, which matches the sense of perfect and imagined.

clue.text: Entering bar, there is drunk with bishop and right little yapper!

indicators.note: the mixed letters and the bishop go inside the name of a chocolate bar

parts.note: a Yorkie is a chunky British chocolate bar

indicators.note: drunk letters are reeling about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone drunk walks into a pub with a bishop and a noisy small dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a British chocolate bar, as in this puzzle's other 'bar' clues; 'drunk' scrambles THERE IS into SHIRETE and 'Entering' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small, feisty breed of terrier famed for barking, so a little dog that yaps.

clue.text: Shape-shifter tries to shift after a little time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the abbreviation for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so the letters of tries are rearranged

explanation.surface: A changeling attempts to move on after a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shape-shifter' suggests a mythical creature, but it is the video game in which falling blocks are turned and shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: In this classic puzzle video game the player rotates and moves falling block shapes, so it shifts shapes.

clue.text: Symbol of the British nation, not that it will crumble, all may conclude?

parts.note: the opposite of that is this

indicators.note: each of the preceding words gives its last letter, the ending of them all

explanation.surface: A national emblem may fall apart, everyone might decide.
explanation.walkthrough: The British nation meant is Scotland, one of the nations of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly purple flower is Scotland's national emblem, and Scotland is a nation within Britain.

clue.text: Fresh start for rider, as pedestrian

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced by a new one

parts.note: a biker rides a motorcycle

explanation.surface: A cyclist begins again, this time on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh start' changes only the first letter of BIKER, giving H in place of B.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian, as a noun, is someone travelling on foot, which a rambler or walker does.

clue.text: See 26
The cracks in slippery surface required further assessment

indicators.note: the broken-up word goes inside the word for an ice surface

parts.note: a rink is a sheet of ice for skating

indicators.note: the word The cracks, breaking apart into a new order of its letters

explanation.surface: Cracks in the ice meant the rink needed another inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' looks like a noun, but it is a verb telling the word The to break up, into ETH, before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider a plan is to assess it again, so a second look or reappraisal.

clue.text: Stuffed in general election, bitter

indicators.note: the letters are packed inside the words that follow, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: Someone sore at ballot-box stuffing in a national vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like an adjective for a loser, but it is a British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a British style of hoppy draught beer, a kind of this brew.

clue.text: Those charging club, perhaps, as one selling pork pies?

parts.note: bulls are the animals that charge
a club is one example of something that strikes

explanation.surface: Charging animals and a weapon, describing a butcher's shop selling pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pies' is rhyming slang for lies, so the seller is a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse word for someone who talks nonsense or tells lies, and pork pies means lies.

clue.text: Series of bars as animal restraint, ultimately — walker free?

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: only the final letter of restraint is kept

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with, whimsically a walker
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Metal bars hold animals back, yet a hiker passes freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walker' looks like a rambler, but it is a LEG, the limb that walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced metal bars set over a pit in a road stop hooved livestock crossing, though people and vehicles pass.

clue.text: Salt, surfeit going over a friend

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a glut is an excess
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Too much salt making a pal sick.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a salt of glutamic acid, as in the flavour enhancer monosodium glutamate.

clue.text: Illegal drugs in clothing

definitions.meaning: slang for narcotics, especially heroin or cannabis
informal word for clothes or outfit

explanation.surface: Drugs hidden in someone's garments.
explanation.definitionFit: The same slang word means both drugs and one's togs, the clothes one wears.

clue.text: Where King John's powers were diluted with weak alcoholic drink, say?

definitions.text: Where King John's powers were diluted

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard, not spelt, the same

parts.note: a watery honey wine would be a runny mead

explanation.surface: A historical quiz: where the king lost power, and with a watery drink.
explanation.walkthrough: King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215 in a meadow by the Thames, curbing royal power.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadow beside the Thames where Magna Carta limited the king's authority in 1215.

clue.text: Might one be popped in quotes, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something gets popped inside quotation marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popped' points to proposing marriage: one 'pops' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposing marriage is known as popping it, the big inquiry asked of a partner.

clue.text: Beauty got to her feet?

definitions.meaning: a lovely flower, a classic emblem of beauty
stood up, past tense of the verb meaning to stand

explanation.surface: A lovely woman stood up.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower is the type of beauty, and the past of the verb to stand up is the same word.

clue.text: Novel on crack, the whole thing?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel
a bang is a loud crack

explanation.surface: A book about drugs, covering everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug, but it is a sharp noise.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'the whole shebang', the word means the entire affair or everything involved.

clue.text: There's silence after one's pushed flexible tube into sheep

indicators.note: the reshaped letters are pushed inside the meat word

parts.note: mutton is the meat of sheep

indicators.note: flexible means bendy, so the letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: A vet pushes a bendy tube into a sheep and silence follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' bends the tube's letters into EBUT; 'pushed' belongs to the definition, the press of a control, not to the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing this control on a phone or remote cuts the sound, so quiet follows a press.

clue.text: See 5
Those crowned heads in outrageous leotards entering bar

indicators.note: the initials go into the name of a chocolate bar

parts.note: a Mars bar is a popular chocolate bar

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next two words is taken

explanation.surface: Royalty in garish leotards walk into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those crowned' suggests royalty, but teeth are given crowns by dentists.
explanation.definitionFit: Back grinding teeth often get a dental crown fitted over them, so they are crowned.

clue.text: Attitude in US puritans abandoning lake for capital city

indicators.note: the attitude word goes inside the trimmed word for puritans
the lake letter is dropped from the word for puritans

parts.note: bluenoses is American slang for prudish moralists
an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: American prudes leave a lake behind, bringing an attitude with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluenoses is American slang for prudes, a word few solvers outside the US will know; 'abandoning' drops the lake's letter from it.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American metropolis is the seat of government of Argentina.

clue.text: Service industry job ends up in a class of its own

definitions.text: in a class of its own

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A job in the service sector that is unmatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAF plus Y and B around, giving BYFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is the best by a wide margin means it is unrivalled, way ahead.

clue.text: River, perfect river

parts.note: to hone is to refine and perfect

explanation.surface: A river described as ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'River' is the abbreviation; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A major French waterway flowing from the Alps to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Fish, one in a warm stream?

definitions.meaning: a flat sea fish related to the skate
a beam of light is one of many in a stream of sunshine

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in a warm current.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat fish shares its name with a single beam of light, one of those in sunshine.

clue.text: A god involved in heinous act as entering bar, not a ripple to be seen

definitions.text: not a ripple to be seen

indicators.note: the whole assembly goes inside the name of a chocolate bar

parts.note: a Flake is a crumbly Cadbury chocolate bar

indicators.note: the god is wrapped inside the scrambled letters
heinous means wicked, so the letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A god commits a terrible deed while entering a pub, leaving calm waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a British chocolate bar, not a pub; 'heinous' scrambles ACT AS into TASCA, which is 'involved in' the god, and 'entering' puts all of it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something completely level, like a calm sea with no waves at all.

clue.text: Hole provided between gold and diamonds

indicators.note: the word for provided sits between gold and diamonds

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
ice is slang for diamonds
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A jewel setting: a hole made between the gold and the diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or aperture in the body or a device, such as a mouth or vent.

clue.text: Surgeries' tender, qualified as medical worker

indicators.note: qualified means modified, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A clinic's carer passed exams to work in medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualified' seems to describe a trained worker, but it signals that the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A state-certified nurse is a health professional working in hospitals and clinics.
